entities.summary:
3 (three) is a number, numeral, and digit with religious and cultural significance in many societies. It is the natural number following 2 and preceding 4, and is the smallest odd prime number and the only prime preceding a square number. This numerical value has been a source of fascination and reverence across various cultures and civilizations, from ancient Babylon to modern times. In many religious traditions, three is considered a sacred number, symbolizing the Trinity, the Holy Trinity, or the Three Jewels of Buddhism.

As a numerical value, 3 has played a significant role in the development of mathematics, particularly in the study of geometry and algebra. It is a fundamental element in the construction of triangles, which have been a cornerstone of mathematics and science for centuries. The Pythagorean theorem, which states that the square of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides, is a direct application of the number 3.

In addition to its mathematical significance, 3 has also been a powerful symbol in various cultures, representing the concept of unity, completeness, and perfection. In many ancient cultures, three was considered a sacred number, representing the connection between heaven and earth, the three aspects of the human personality, or the three stages of life. This symbolism can be seen in various forms of art, architecture, and literature, from the three-headed gods of ancient Greece to the three aspects of the human soul in Buddhist philosophy.

The significance of 3 extends beyond its numerical value, as it has also played a crucial role in shaping human history, culture, and society. From the three wise men who visited the newborn Jesus to the three aspects of the human condition, 3 has been a recurring theme in human experience, representing the complexities and nuances of human nature.
